messages.settings.diag.recovery.title: Recovery guide
messages.settings.diag.recovery.authBody:
Bearer: mebular token grant --scope memory.read,memory.admin
OAuth: static token → 401 invalid token
/register → 404 without both secrets:
MEBULAR_OAUTH_ADMIN_SECRET / MEBULAR_OAUTH_REGISTER_SECRET
Fix: mcp.http.auth=none in config.json (loopback only), restart mebular serve.
messages.settings.diag.recovery.hostBody:
Non-loopback needs auth≠none + TLS + certificates, or serve will not start.
Use 127.0.0.1, or supply all three and restart.
messages.settings.diag.recovery.certBody:
tls=true without tlsKey/tlsCert: startup fails with MCP_INSECURE_CONFIG (no silent downgrade).
Add both paths, or turn TLS off.
messages.settings.diag.recovery.consoleBody:
Check mebular status and the serve log.
MCP_STORAGE_LOCKED: another instance holds the lock.
MCP_INSECURE_CONFIG: bad host/auth/TLS combination.

messages.security.downgrade.codeIntro: Downgrading from Medium needs the 6-digit code from this device.

messages.security.approval.whySafe: The pairing code never travels over any channel: both devices derive it from the action digest, so a human comparison is enough.

messages.security.totp.seed.title: Authenticator seed
messages.security.totp.seed.warningDefault: The seed is the key to this tier: whoever sees it can pass the code. Show it in person only between devices you own.

messages.security.totp.show.title: Show authenticator seed
messages.security.totp.show.intro: Enter this device’s code once before showing the seed (stops a casual glance).
messages.security.totp.generate.title: Generate a shared authenticator seed?
messages.security.totp.generate.body: Only root can generate it. The new seed is written on this device; import it on your other devices so the Medium gate applies consistently.
messages.security.recovery.once.warning: This code shows only once. Copy it to offline media (paper, metal or a password tool), apart from the master key backup. Do not screenshot or send it in chat. If lost, rotate it.
messages.security.recovery.once.after: Choose the button below once you have copied it; once this view is gone it cannot be shown again.
messages.security.recovery.rotate.title: Rotate recovery code
messages.security.recovery.rotate.body: Sign with the current recovery code to get a new one. Signatures with the old code stop working at once (history already accepted is not reverted).
messages.security.recovery.rotate.help: The new code is shown once; have your offline media ready.
messages.security.recovery.rotate.newIntro: Old keyId {keyId} has been rotated; new signatures with the old code are no longer accepted.
messages.security.recovery.generate.title: Generate a recovery code?
messages.security.recovery.generate.body: A recovery code replaces a High co-sign when no other device is present. It shows once; have offline media ready.
messages.security.recovery.error.mismatch: The recovery code does not match the current keyId (it may have been rotated): use the latest code.
messages.security.recovery.error.missing: No recovery code yet: generate or rotate one from the security card first.
messages.security.recovery.error.invalid: Invalid recovery code format: enter all 34 characters (hyphens optional).
messages.security.recovery.error.notApplicable: Not at the High tier: a recovery code only replaces a High co-sign and is not needed here.
messages.security.recovery.error.signFailed: Recovery code signature check failed: retry; if it keeps failing, rotate the code.
messages.security.recovery.code.label: Recovery code
messages.security.recovery.code.help: The 34-character code you stored offline. It signs locally only: never uploaded, never stored in the browser. The field clears on submit.
messages.security.revoke.viaRecovery.title: Remove device · recovery code
messages.security.revoke.viaRecovery.intro: Currently High · device co-sign. Sign locally with the offline recovery code to write the removal record immediately; the code never passes through the cloud.

messages.security.tier.viaRecovery.intro: Currently High · device co-sign. Sign this downgrade with the offline recovery code; the code never passes through the cloud.
messages.security.revoke.title: Remove device
messages.security.revoke.bodyIntro: Records signed by {device} are no longer accepted here, and this device stops sending it data. Already synced data is not reclaimed; another device can restore it.
messages.security.revoke.gate.high: High · device co-sign: another admitted device must compare the pairing code and approve; this device then finishes the removal automatically.
messages.security.revoke.gate.medium: Currently Medium · authenticator code: the next step asks for this device’s 6-digit code.
messages.security.revoke.intro: Policy records signed by {device} will no longer be accepted here; it runs automatically once the co-sign is approved.
messages.security.revoke.codeIntro: Enter this device’s 6-digit code to write the removal record.
messages.security.restore.title: Restore device
messages.security.restore.bodyIntro: {device} will be accepted here again. Restoring starts a new epoch: records it signed before (subscriptions, removals and so on) do not come back, and it must re-declare subscriptions.
messages.security.restore.gate.high: High · device co-sign: another admitted device must compare the pairing code and approve; this device then finishes the restore automatically.
messages.security.restore.intro: {device} will be restored; policy records from the old epoch do not come back.
messages.security.restore.viaRecovery.title: Restore device · recovery code
messages.security.restore.viaRecovery.intro: Sign locally with the offline recovery code to write the restore record immediately; the code never passes through the cloud.
messages.security.restore.codeIntro: Enter this device’s 6-digit code to write the restore record.
messages.settings.write.restarting: Restarting automatically to apply the configuration…
messages.settings.write.rolledBack: New configuration not in effect: rolled back (see banner / Advanced · Diagnostics)
messages.settings.restart.confirmBody:
Restart the local daemon (mebular serve) to apply pending settings.
The console is briefly unavailable and reloads when it's back. Continue?
messages.settings.restart.triggered: Restart triggered, waiting for the daemon…

messages.assistants.empty: No assistants registered yet: choose “+ Add assistant” to start.
messages.assistants.failed.label: Connection failed
messages.assistants.verify.pending: Wired up — takes effect after you restart {name}
messages.assistants.verify.pendingWithNote: Wired up — takes effect after you restart {name} ({note})
messages.assistants.verify.pendingSteps: ① Quit the app completely (end the process, not just the window) ② open it again ③ mebular should be in its tool list. We never restart it for you.
messages.assistants.verify.failed: Verification failed: fix the failed step above, then choose “Verify again”.
messages.assistants.detail.configOnly: Config-level check only (no verification command for this assistant)

messages.assistants.form.modeSnippet: Paste a snippet (snippet only, merge by hand)
messages.assistants.form.name: Name

messages.assistants.action.verifyReady: Configuration is ready — restart the app to take effect, then choose “I reloaded, verify”.
messages.assistants.action.verifyNotPassed: Verification failed: expand to see the failed step and its output.
messages.assistants.action.copied: Snippet copied; paste it into the assistant’s MCP configuration.
messages.assistants.preview.unchanged: (identical to the current configuration, no change needed)
messages.assistants.rollback.title: Roll back the assistant configuration?
messages.assistants.rollback.body: Restores the assistant’s configuration from the automatic pre-connect backup. This overwrites the Mebular entry written when connecting.
messages.assistants.done.connectChanged: Connected (original configuration backed up). Takes effect after you restart the assistant.
messages.assistants.form.error.id: The ID must be lowercase kebab-case (for example my-assistant)
messages.assistants.form.error.name: Name is required
messages.assistants.form.error.path: Configuration file path is required (file mode)
messages.assistants.remove.title: Remove the custom assistant?
messages.assistants.remove.body: Removes the registration of “{id}”; its configuration file is untouched. Register it again to reconnect.

messages.authToken.note: This MCP connection uses bearer auth. Paste a token to continue. The token stays in this browser only.
messages.authToken.label: Access token
messages.authToken.help: Generate one in the terminal with {command}.
messages.attention.title: Needs attention
messages.domains.title: Memory sharing
messages.domains.note:
Who you share with and what you share, at a glance.
Create a memory domain and record alone; open it to see subscribers. Devices not in a cloud get no data.
messages.domains.detail.relationNone: No other devices subscribe to this domain
messages.domains.detail.noSubscribers: No subscriptions yet (each device decides for itself)
messages.domains.detail.subscribersHint: Each device decides for itself; the graph records it from this device’s view.
messages.domains.rejoin.note: This device left and its watermark was cleared: after resync, peers resend the domain from the start (or an initial snapshot).
messages.domains.rejoin.title: Peers will resend this domain from the start
messages.domains.rejoin.confirmBody: Reset “{namespace}”: clears the local watermark and peers resend the domain from the start (or an initial snapshot). Rejected if this device is not subscribed. Continue?
messages.domains.subscribe.title: Receiving every update and syncing this device’s additions to other subscribers
messages.domains.subscribe.note: Subscribe to receive every update in this domain; this device’s additions sync to other subscribers (read + upkeep).
messages.domains.task.note: Task plane: the initiator roots a dispatched task tree; remote agents run tasks and return results (a DAG). Subscribe to send and receive here.
messages.domains.handoff.action: Leave and hand off this domain…
messages.domains.handoff.hint: Clears only this device’s data and watermark; needs the successor’s ack. Data synced elsewhere is not rolled back.
messages.domains.unsubscribeSome.title: Subscribe to only some memory domains
messages.domains.unsubscribeSome.body: Currently subscribed to all memory domains. After unsubscribing “{namespace}”, only the other {count} stay subscribed; new domains default to unsubscribed.
messages.domains.create.error.empty: Enter a memory domain name first.
messages.domains.create.success: Created and subscribed to “{namespace}”; this device can start recording now
messages.handoff.title: Leave and hand off · {namespace}
messages.handoff.desc:
Leave and hand off: this device erases the domain’s data and watermark (no tombstone; __policy__ kept).
The successor must ack everything first, or the handoff aborts. To resend from the start, resubscribe.
messages.handoff.descStatic:
Leave and hand off: this device erases the domain’s data and watermark (no tombstone; __policy__ kept).
The successor must ack everything first, or the handoff aborts. To resend from the start, resubscribe.
messages.handoff.confirmBody: Hand “{namespace}” to {successor} and erase the domain from this device (irreversible). Data synced elsewhere is not rolled back. Continue?
messages.audit.title: Audit timeline
messages.audit.event.restore: By {issuer}: restored device {subject} (old-epoch policy records stay retired){extra}
messages.audit.event.revoke: By {issuer}: removed device {subject} (this device no longer accepts its policy records){extra}
messages.audit.event.handoff: By {issuer}: handed {namespace} to {subject}{forced} · {count} not covered

messages.memories.note.archiveBody: = put away and no longer recalled; restore anytime;
messages.memories.note.deleteAfter: ; deleted memories no longer appear in any recall by default.
messages.memories.empty: No matching memories (deleted/archived are hidden by default; {total} total).
messages.memories.delete.title: Delete memory (irreversible)
messages.memories.delete.body:
Delete {id}: writes a synced tombstone; the memory is no longer recalled by default.
Snapshots already copied by peers cannot be reclaimed. Continue?

messages.deviceCard.interop.noContent: · this domain has no content yet
messages.deviceCard.interop.hidden: {count} more domains are unsubscribed on both sides

messages.deviceCard.help.elevated: After removal this device no longer accepts its records; data already synced is not reclaimed. {gate}

messages.deviceCard.help.gateMedium: Medium tier requires this device’s 6-digit TOTP code.

messages.deviceCard.peer.title: Memory domains it subscribes to
messages.deviceCard.peer.note: Declared by peer · recorded on the map
messages.deviceCard.toast.sync: Sync triggered (a session starts at once when there is pending data)
messages.deviceCard.reset.title: Reset sync watermarks
messages.deviceCard.reset.body: Clears local sync watermarks with {device}. Synced content is not rolled back; at most, confirmed events are resent once.

messages.about.title: About this device
messages.about.loading: Loading this device… (if it stays like this, check that serve is running)
messages.about.locked.title: This device is not initialized yet
messages.about.locked.desc: Create or join a cloud to see identity, storage and runtime here; nothing is guessed while locked.
messages.about.identity.title: Identity & storage
messages.about.identity.renameNote: Only you can change it. It syncs to other devices in the same cloud; certificates are not reissued.
messages.about.identity.renameSuccess: Device name changed to “{name}”; it syncs to other devices in the same cloud.
messages.about.identity.modeDelegated: delegated (delegated certificate chain, no master key)
messages.about.identity.modeRoot: root (holds the user master key and can issue certificates to any device)
messages.about.convergence.title: Convergence health
messages.about.convergence.summary: Peers {peers} · converged {ok} · stalled {stalled} · diverged {diverged} · unverified {unverifiable} · offline {offline}
messages.about.convergence.note: Derived from state-fingerprint reconciliation; differences only raise warnings and do not change subscriptions or sync.
messages.about.syncRate.title: Sync cadence
messages.about.syncRate.tag: Read-only · on by default; keep it on
messages.about.syncRate.note: On by default; keep it on. To change it, edit sync.autoSync / sync.pushOnWrite in config.json.
messages.about.statusOnly.title: Read-only status (derived)
messages.about.statusOnly.desc:
Set at runtime: relay pool, LAN discovery, bridge, hole punching, broadcast, join, TLS.
The console shows real values and reasons; nothing here is editable.
messages.about.runtime.title: Runtime status
messages.about.runtime.pendingRestartBody: {count} config changes are saved but not active (this instance keeps the config from its last start; applies after restart)
messages.about.runtime.broadcastOff: Off (opt-in: add __net__ to sync.namespaces or set network.broadcast)
messages.about.runtime.listenAlarm: ⚠ Non-loopback listen addresses ({addresses}). Use loopback / LAN, or a relay, and admit only joined devices in the firewall.
messages.about.paths.title: Peer connection paths
messages.about.paths.empty: No address book entries yet: waiting for pairing hints (invite token) or the first peer connection.
messages.about.paths.note: Paths come from the core address book (direct > lan > relay; failing candidates are replaced with backoff). Read-only; subscriptions are unchanged.
messages.about.fleet.title: Fleet summary
messages.about.fleet.note: Task plane, not a memory domain: the initiator roots a task tree and remote agents return results over the memory channel (a DAG, not a shared pool). Config: fleet CLI + fleet.config.json.
messages.about.tools.title: Capabilities
messages.about.tools.note: Agents call the same handlers over MCP; people call mebular <name>. The GUI only manages the daemon and subscriptions, adding no operations.
messages.namespaceNew.title: New memory domain
messages.namespaceNew.note: You can record alone on this device. New domains are subscribed by default; unsubscribe anytime.
